$adoptionNote: Three kinds of record are declared here, and the first two run in OPPOSITE directions, which is worth reading before the entries. (1) The reference stylesheet — this repository AUTHORS it and four language tiers ship a byte-copy, so `source` is the canonical file and `consumers` are the copies. (2) The PROOF KIT (Phase 1754) — this repository is the kit's first ADOPTER, so the canonical file lives in the kit's repository and the copy is the one here. The registry compares two named files and reports any difference whichever side moved, which is exactly the drift check an adopter wants; what it cannot express is which side is canonical, so every kit record says so in its `regen`: the remedy is always to re-copy FROM the kit's repository, never to push a change the other way. The kit's own manifest carries these entries as `$sources`, inert, with the consumer path left for an adopter to fill; they are filled HERE rather than there because an adopter must be able to adopt without editing the repository it is adopting from. `check` is `bytes` for the pin — a pin is a hash-verified declaration and a byte is a byte — and `fingerprint` for the rest, which are text two platforms may legitimately check out with different line endings. (3) The PROGRAM MODELS and the demanded corpus (fuaran#2012) — the bounded program core's UI adapter moved here with the two proof claims about it, so the program repository is canonical for the copied models, their extractions and the demanded corpus, exactly as the kit's repository is for the kit: each record's `regen` says which way to copy.
